title: Bank reconciliation
examples: What is the difference between the cash book balance and the bank statement balance?
If the bank forgets a payment, how do I fix my records?
When should I perform a bank reconciliation?

explain.say: Today we learn to check our bank records against the bank statement.
First we look at unpresented cheques. These are cheques we wrote but the bank has not paid yet.

draw.text: Unpresented Cheques: Written but not cleared

explain.say: If we wrote a cheque but the payee hasn't cashed it, we must add it back to the bank statement balance.
Next we check for bank errors. Sometimes the bank makes a mistake when recording transactions.

draw.text: Bank Errors: Mistakes by the bank

explain.say: If the bank incorrectly debits your account, you must add that amount back to the bank statement balance.
In real life, you reconcile your bank account every month to ensure your records are accurate.

faq.q: What is the main purpose of a bank reconciliation?
faq.a: It is a process to ensure that the balance in your records matches the bank's records. This helps you find any differences or errors.
asks: Why do I need to reconcile my bank account?
What is the goal of this process?

faq.q: How do I treat unpresented cheques?
faq.a: Unpresented cheques are cheques you have written but the recipient has not yet deposited or cashed. You add these amounts back to the bank statement balance.
asks: What if I write a cheque but it's not cashed?
Should I add unpresented cheques to my books?

faq.q: What kind of bank errors should I look out for?
faq.a: You should look for instances where the bank has either added money you did not receive or taken money you did not spend. These require adjustments.
asks: What if the bank takes the wrong amount?
Are there common bank mistakes I should know?

faq.q: Do I adjust my cash book when I find a bank error?
faq.a: No, you only adjust the bank statement balance when preparing the reconciliation statement. You must make a separate journal entry in your cash book.
asks: Does finding an error mean I change my cash book?
Where do I record the correction?

faq.q: Is it enough to just check the dates?
faq.a: No, checking dates is not enough. You must check the amounts and the nature of the transactions to find all discrepancies.
asks: Is matching dates enough for reconciliation?
What else besides dates should I check?

facts: A bank reconciliation compares the balance in the company's books with the bank statement balance.
Unpresented cheques are cheques issued by the business but not yet presented to the bank.
If the bank incorrectly debits an account, the amount must be added back to the bank statement balance.
The goal is to find the true, correct cash balance.

quiz.say: The cheques you have written but the bank has not yet paid are called:
quiz.why: These cheques are recorded in your books but haven't cleared the bank yet, so they must be added back.

wrong.0: These cheques have been paid, so they need no adjustment.
wrong.2: These cheques have already been processed by the bank and should already be accounted for.
wrong.3: These are deductions made by the bank, not cheques you wrote.

quiz.say: If the bank statement shows a debit for a service fee you never used, what should you do?

options.show: Subtract the amount from the bank balance
options.say: Subtract the amount from the bank balance

options.show: Record it as a sales income
options.say: Record it as a sales income

options.show: Add the amount back to the bank balance
options.say: Add the amount back to the bank balance

quiz.why: Since the bank wrongly reduced your money, you must add it back to find the correct balance.

wrong.0: Subtracting it again would mean you are losing money twice.
wrong.1: You cannot ignore the bank statement because it shows what really happened.
wrong.2: This changes the nature of the transaction entirely.

quiz.say: If the bank statement shows a direct deposit for a customer payment, how do you adjust your records?

options.show: Add it to the unpresented cheques
options.say: Add it to the unpresented cheques

options.show: Add the amount to the cash book balance
options.say: Add the amount to the cash book balance

options.show: Subtract the amount from the cash book balance
options.say: Subtract the amount from the cash book balance

quiz.why: A direct deposit increases your money, so you must record this increase in your own books.

wrong.0: Ignoring it means your books will not match the bank statement.
wrong.1: This confuses a deposit with a cheque that hasn't cleared.
wrong.3: Subtracting it would incorrectly show that you lost money.
